name: S2-COMPRESSED-ACT row 6: the first bootable clip act — the opening stretch of Emerald Hill Zone act 1
note: WHY THIS RECTANGLE. (1) It is the act's FULL WIDTH — three sections, 6144 px, all of grid_w. Parcel 6 painted two sections and parcel 7 measured what that cost: at x=4096 the art and both collision planes stopped dead and the player walked off the painted world into 2048 px of void. The owner reported exactly that edge ("the foreground just randomly ends at that 409x spot") and chose to fill the act rather than shrink it, so the clip now reaches the camera's own EDGE_CLAMP bound and there is nothing past the ground to walk into. (2) Its height is 1024 and not 2048 because EHZ's whole crop is 128 tiles tall (zone.json extent.crop_tiles) and R9 refuses a rect past it — so the act's lower two section rows stay air, and a fall still has no bottom (see unpainted_remainder.unbounded_fall). (3) src == dst, so the paste SHIFT is (0,0): R12's 16-px block quantum is satisfied by construction, and a collision misalignment — which moves ground 8 px and which no screenshot shows — cannot hide behind a nonzero shift here. (4) dst (0,0) puts painted geometry in SECTION 0, which is the section whose block blob and local map own the map.toml head labels (OJZ_Sec0_Blocks / OJZ_Sec0_LocalMap); an all-air section 0 would content-dedup into an `equ` alias of some other section and the placement rows would name a label that is not a section head. (5) It is the opening of Emerald Hill act 1 — flat ground under the whole spawn column, the first hill, palm trees — which is the most recognisable ground in Sonic 2 and therefore the clearest possible answer to 'is this our engine drawing Sonic 2'. (6) EHZ has ZERO cells on CRAM line 0 (verified in its zone.json counts, not assumed), so the palette defect parcel 2 measured in CPZ and WFZ cannot appear here. (7) EHZ itself is six sections wide (12288 px), so three sections is a CROP of available content, not all of it — a wider act could take more.

unpainted_remainder.why: NOTHING IS UNPAINTED ON THE X AXIS. 6144 is the act's own width (grid_w 3 x SECTION_SIZE 2048), so this names the end of the act rather than an edge inside it: the painted foreground runs to the last column the camera can reach, and EDGE_CLAMP stops the camera there. Parcel 6 painted 4096 of those 6144 px and parcel 7 measured the consequence — at x=4096 the art and BOTH collision planes stopped dead, top to bottom, because the tile cache carries the nametable and both planes in the same block, and the player walked off the painted world and fell the act's full height. Parcel 8 filled the remaining section instead of shrinking the act to fit the clip (the owner's call). The declaration is KEPT rather than deleted because it is two-sided: clip_reachability.py refuses if the painted world ends anywhere but exactly x=6144, so if a future re-bake loses a section this says so instead of a report describing it later. THE Y AXIS IS A DIFFERENT STORY and is not fixed by this — see unbounded_fall below.

unbounded_fall.why: THE ACT STILL HAS NO BOTTOM. 744 of the 768 painted columns have air below their LAST landing surface, so a body that gets under the terrain has no floor anywhere in the 6144 px act and falls forever. (The other 24 are the pit at x 4672..4863, which has no landing surface at all to get under — they are counted in floorless_columns instead.) It is not a conversion defect: Sonic 2's terrain interiors are LRB-only ($2000 - solid left/right/bottom and NOTHING to a falling body), and Sonic 2 survives that with a LEVEL BOTTOM BOUNDARY that kills and restarts. EHZ act 1 declares its own at y=800 (s2_donor.level_size -> (0, 10656, 0, 800)). A clip act declares none, because the act it is baked into is the shipped OJZ act whose descriptor is hand-written and shared with the canonical ROM — and because this engine has no death of any kind yet, so there is nothing for a bottom boundary to do. The count rose from 512 to 744 when parcel 8 widened the clip from two sections to three: more painted ground means more columns whose interior a body can get under, which is the honest arithmetic and not a regression. THE COUNT IS THE CHECK: add a floor, a death plane or a bottom boundary and it drops, and this gate says so.

floorless_columns.why: EMERALD HILL ACT 1'S OWN BOTTOMLESS PIT, AT x 4672..4863. This is not a hole in the conversion — it is Sonic 2 level design, faithfully carried across: the art is fully drawn in all 128 cells of every one of those columns (you SEE a pit), the collision cells are present, and they are the pit's LRB-only walls, so no column in the run carries a SOLID_TOP surface at any height on either plane. Sonic 2 ships this pit and survives it with the level bottom boundary at y=800 recorded in unbounded_fall above, which kills and restarts a player who falls in. THIS ENGINE HAS NO DEATH AT ALL, so here the same pit is an endless fall. It entered the act when parcel 8 widened the clip to the act's full width on the owner's instruction; the alternative was stopping the clip at x=4672, which just moves the hard edge he reported from 4096 to 4672. Declared rather than refused because refusing would refuse faithful donor data for a hazard the donor game itself ships. Plane B is NOT declared and deliberately so: it is unreachable in this act (no crossover mark), its holes stay informational, and the day something writes the player's layer byte they become a failure by name.
